newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Council to hold off on Kalanke job-preference rules.
newsitem.headline: Council to hold off on Kalanke job-preference rules.

text.p: Most ministers at the Social Affairs Council on Monday agreed they should hold off on amending the EU's equal opportunities directive, EU officials said.
They were discussing a draft directive, COM(96)93, to amend the existing law to clarify the European Court of Justice's "Kalanke" ruling, which declared a German quota scheme illegal.
But most ministers argued either that the legislation was unnecessary since the court ruling spoke for itself or that it was premature, officials said.

The European court ruled last October that a quota system enacted by the German state of Bremen violated the equal opportunities directive by giving women with the same qualifications as men "absolute and unconditional" priority for jobs in categories where they were under-represented.
The European Commission proposed legislation to amend the equal opportunities directive, 76/207/EEC, in an effort to ensure that the Kalanke ruling was not interpreted too broadly.
Its text would assure employers that they could adopt schemes to boost the number of women who are hired or promoted as long as they did not turn into rigid quotas.
However, only Spain, Italy and Ireland supported that plan at the Council, one official said.
Sweden wanted to go further by allowing more aggressive schemes for promoting women, he added. But most others agreed that no action should be taken now, officials said.

Ministers said the Council should wait for another Court of Justice ruling that is expected to clarify further the question of women's job preferences and for the outcome of discussions on equal opportunity issues at the inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms, they said.
